Once upon a time, three Billy Goats lived on a hill.
They were the Billy Goats Gruff.
Little Billy was the smallest, Middle Billy was a bit bigger, and Big Billy was the biggest of all.
Uh-oh!
The grass on their hill was nearly all gone.
But across the river there was a meadow full of yummy green grass.
To get to the meadow, the goats had to cross a little wooden bridge.
And under the bridge lived a grumpy Troll, with eyes as big as saucers and a nose as long as a carrot.
He sat there all by himself, day after day.
Little Billy went first.
Trip, trap, trip, trap, went his little hooves on the bridge.
Who's that trip-trapping over my bridge?
said Troll.
It's only me, Little Billy Goat Gruff,
said Little Billy in a teeny-tiny voice.
I'm going to the meadow to munch some grass.
Nobody crosses my bridge without a stamping match!
Oh, please let me cross,
said Little Billy.
I'm too little to stamp.
Wait for my big brother.
He's much bigger than me!
Oh, all right then, off you go!
And Little Billy skipped across the bridge to the meadow.
Next came Middle Billy.
Trip, trap, trip, trap, went his hooves on the bridge.
It's only me, Middle Billy Goat Gruff,
said Middle Billy.
And Middle Billy trotted across the bridge to the meadow.
Last of all came Big Billy.
TRIP, TRAP, TRIP, TRAP, went his big hooves on the bridge.
The whole bridge shook and shook!
It's me, Big Billy Goat Gruff,
said Big Billy in a big, deep voice.
said Troll, and he stomped up onto the bridge.
Stamp, stamp, stamp, went his big bare feet.
Big Billy stood very still and waited for his turn.
But the old boards were wet and slippery.
Whoops!
The Troll wibbled and wobbled, this way and that way.
Splash, splash, splash!
He slid off the low bridge and sat down in the shallow river.
Are you okay?
said Big Billy.
The water was nice and cool, and it only came up to the Troll's tummy.
A little fish tickled his toes, and he started to giggle.
Ho, ho, ho! That tickles!
And the three Billy Goats laughed too.
The soggy Troll climbed out onto the bank at the bottom of the hill and sat down.
Big Billy came down off the bridge and sat next to him.
Why are you so grumpy?
I think you're just lonely.
Nobody ever asks me to come along,
Come across with us and try the yummy green grass,
So Big Billy and the Troll walked across the bridge, side by side, to the other goats in the meadow.
The Troll nibbled a little bit of grass.
Mmm, mmm, mmm!
It was so yummy that he gave a great big, happy smile.
Thank you, Billy Goats,
This is the best day ever!
After that, the three Billy Goats Gruff and their new friend munched yummy green grass all summer long.
Every evening the goats went trip, trap, trip, trap, home over the bridge, and the Troll waved goodnight.
Come back tomorrow!
Snip, snap, snout, this tale's told out.
